fields.v: Metrics: F1 / EM% / SQL valid% / AST exact% / AST sim / runnable%; models not stated for Stage 2. Success criterion: none stated by the authors (metrics are similarity to reference PostgreSQL scripts and runnability, with no threshold). Stage 1: authors' pipeline + custom agent loop + GPT-oss-120b and GPT-o4-mini (not separated): 623/1,006 regenerated (61.9%), 380/623 executed (61.0%); tables ~85%; ~2,000 tokens per iteration, ~3 iterations per object. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors (they call the pipeline 'feasible'); cost: no criterion stated by the authors. Stage 2 native baseline (Table I = Table III diagonal): (1) Kiro spec + Kiro + n.s.: 0.365/0.33/33.74/0.33/0.207/0.72. (2) Spec Kit + Copilot + n.s.: 0.75/13.15/43.51/12.76/0.257/0. (3) Antigravity + Gemini + n.s.: 0.73/13.32/45.54/12.98/0.69/2.22. (12) Gemini spec -> Copilot: 0.665/12.8/63/19.9/0.514/runnable not implemented. Copilot spec -> Kiro/Gemini: not evaluated. (16) RAG -> Gemini: 0.57/13.40/13.82/20.20/0.32/1.80. (17) RAG -> Copilot: 0.69/12.76/43.51/12.99/0.285/0.28. For every Stage 2 configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured
fields.quote: These measures intentionally distinguish lexical, syntactic, structural, and operational quality.
fields.why: The authors state no success criterion or threshold for any metric, so the works/partly/does-not-work verdicts (and the Stage 1 cost verdict) are extractor thresholds and should be "no criterion stated by the authors".
fields.doubt: Os veredictos "Partly", "Does not work" e "cost works" não vêm do artigo: os autores só listam métricas (pág. 7) sem limiar de sucesso. Pela regra de 23-11, troca por "no criterion stated by the authors" e mantém os valores. Confirma na secção VI e decide.

fields.v: Spec-first. Authors' wording: 'specification-first migration pipeline'; specification as 'an intermediate representation between software intent and implementation'; Stage 2 native workflows (Kiro, Spec Kit, Antigravity) generate the spec, then code from it
fields.quote: First, a specification-first migration pipeline was evaluated on 1,006 PL/SQL files, of which 623 were successfully regenerated and 380 generated scripts executed successfully in PostgreSQL 16.
fields.why: "Not stated" is not one of the allowed SDD levels, and the authors themselves call the approach specification-first, so the level can be classified (spec-first) with their wording.
fields.doubt: "Not stated" não é um nível válido (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source ou not classifiable). Os autores chamam ao pipeline "specification-first" (resumo, pág. 1) e a spec só serve para gerar o código. Vê a pág. 1 e a Fig. 3 (pág. 6-7) e decide: proponho Spec-first.
